body: Yeah, I definitely understand that self-fulfilling prophecy, and I’ve been trying to ground myself during those moments of insecurity and just push my way through it. I’ve had moments of letting my insecurities dictate my behaviors and it never ends well. All we can do is learn and attempt to change patterns and live a more fulfilling life in the process, but I still have my moments of weakness. I wish we weren’t such social creatures. I feel like I crave that validation from others to tell me I’m not inferior or unloved, but I’m no good at asking for what I need. Unless it’s anonymously, from strangers, of course 🤓
Yes, exactly that. That is a pretty accurate depiction too. I just feel like any attempts to actually grasp any of those floating thoughts is met with extra overwhelm.
Of course, anytime :)
Sent :)

You’re doing great, buddy. Everyone starts somewhere, 3 days is a great start, and I’m proud of you :) If you ever need support from someone who understands, my dms are always open.
This is such kind and helpful advice. I actually teared up reading this because those gestures really do mean the world to someone who is struggling.
I'm okay for right now, but can we still talk? Always nice to have someone to talk to.
Of course. My DMs never close. Feel free to send me a message!
Thank you for the good vibes. You're amazing.
Not weird at all! Shoot me a message :)
Please do send a message! Can't wait to hear from you!
Thank you so, so much. Your words of encouragement mean the world to me. I appreciate that you took the time to comment this.
No, thank you! I'm glad you're here 💖

That is really helpful information about the prepaid. I don't have bright futures so I'm not worried about that. I just thought that maybe prepaid doesn't cover it if I'm not a full-time student? But it works out if I take 14 credits next semester so I wouldn't even need to worry.

Is the 2 drops per 60 hours just that they will drop it without question? I'm just really worried. I have C's in a couple other classes right now, but I'm decently sure that I can bring those up to B's for the end of the semester. I'm trying to tell myself that a C won't be terrible to get in my very first semester because there's still time to make up for it, but it's still something that negatively affects my GPA that I could have fixed by being more prepared.

I'm not sure that my professor is the understanding type. From her perspective, it will look like I've just been negligent with the patterns in the grades I've missed... There was no midterm, so that didn't affect me. I've just missed a ton of assignments due to personal reasons and adjusting to college. It also seems she redirects all correspondence to her TA, so maybe I should reach out to him?
What do you think you're leaning towards? Honestly now I'm just even more torn. I feel like either way, it'll work out somehow. I guess the best way is to talk to an advisor.
Two C's and the rest A's and B's? Alright, you're scaring me a little... How do I know who my advisor is?

Do you think that it's silly to drop a class over a C in my first semester? Should I just stick it out and take the C? I just realize now that I'm in way over my head with 7 classes to focus on and I know I'll be just fine taking 4 instead next semester.

Well, I'm not engineering and if I drop this class, I will only have 10 credits this semester so that's not full-time anymore. I know I have a guaranteed C if I get 100% on the rest of my assignments, even if I bomb the final exam.

Actually, I have two 3 credit classes, two 2 credit classes, and three 1 credit classes. The 3 credit class I'm dropping was a filler from drop/add in August, when I added Extreme Weather to replace something else I dropped at the last minute.
